subcomponents.title: Fixed-canvas uniform viewport fitting

criteria.rationale: computeScale returns one factor, min(availW/designW, availH/designH), floored at MIN_SCALE. Stage applies it as transform: scale(s) on the fixed-size canvas, so the internal composition is never reflowed. The available area is the viewport minus the same STAGE_LAYOUT insets that position the stage area, so the fit uses the stage's real bounds. At 1280×720 browse, avail is 1232×456 and the scale is 1.2. At 390×844 browse, avail is 342×580 and the scale is about 0.389, a 342×148 canvas that fits. Present mode fits too, with avail 1232×568 and 342×692. The browse footer stays under its 200px reserve at 1280×720 with the sample CSS (about 178px, estimated by hand).
evidence: useFitScale.ts computeScale: availW = viewportW − 2·side, availH = viewportH − top − bottom, scale = max(MIN_SCALE, min(availW/designW, availH/designH)).

Before each capture it never confirms data-step-index equals the intended step; it only waits for the index after pressing ArrowRight. Zero captures can therefore still be reported as success.
evidence: inspect-presentation.mjs main(): const count = Number(await page.getAttribute(..., 'data-step-count')); for (let step = 0; step < count; step++) has no !(count > 0) guard.
No read of data-step-index precedes page.screenshot inside the loop.
After the loop it unconditionally prints `[inspect] ${count} screenshots ...` and does not throw when captures is empty.
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: Titles, captions and step order are read from the rendered DOM. The registration check, however, is a regular expression over the registry source text, which is one of the named checks.
evidence: verify.mjs registeredSlugs(): readFileSync(registry source) then text.matchAll(/slug:\s*['"]([^'"]+)['"]/g).
checkRegistry() uses that regex-derived slug list to assert the required presentation is registered.
Titles and captions are read via page.locator('[data-presentation-step-title]') and '[data-presentation-caption]' textContent, but this does not cure the source-regex registration che…
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: Diagnostics and screenshots run for every step. They cover the whole page, including the presentation's chrome.
evidence: inspect-presentation.mjs main(): inside for (step = 0; step < count; step++), each iteration calls page.screenshot({ path: file }) (full viewport, no clip) and page.evaluate(diagnose).
diagnose() selects chrome via '[data-presentation-header] button, [data-presentation-footer] button, [data-presentation-toc-entry], [data-presentation-dot], [data-presentation-attribution]', …
The template copy is identical.
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Skill instructions and templates

criteria.rationale: Templates resolve inside src and match the kit's types. A focused integration test materializes them in a bootstrapped project and builds it.
evidence: scaffold.mjs newPresentation sets KIT = posixRelative(folder, kitDir) and KIT2 from steps/, so imports resolve to src/presentation-kit. The './presentation.css' import resolves because the fi…
Scene.tsx.tmpl passes id and at to Box/Label, and SceneProps and Appear's required children match the kit types. steps/index.ts.tmpl supplies id, era, title, caption, Scene and payload as the Ste…
tests/integration/bootstrap.test.ts bootstraps a project, runs `scaffold.mjs new d added Added`, then runs `npm run build` and `npm run verify`, asserting status 0 and 'rendered added: 2 steps&#3…
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The frontmatter description says when to use the skill. It does not quote example user phrases, and its opening is imperative ('Create or modify a browser presentation...') rather than a third-person statement.
evidence: SKILL.md frontmatter: 'Create or modify a browser presentation ... from a topic, using the and-scene kit. Use when the user asks to make, build, update, or change a presentation (informally, a ta…
The description contains no quoted trigger phrases such as "create a presentation" or "add steps".
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: SKILL.md has no out-of-scope section. None of PowerPoint/Keynote output, PDF or image export, a visual editor, or hosting is listed, and no redirects are given.
evidence: The headings are Procedure (Gather, Resolve target, Generate or modify, Self-verify) and Quality bar; there is no exclusions section.
A read of the whole file shows no mention of PowerPoint, Keynote, PDF export, a visual editor, or hosting.
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: SKILL.md defines no completion-report template. It says only 'state what was run and its outcome' and 'report any remaining advisory warnings accurately'. It does not name the presentation route, the files changed, or the build/render/inspect results as report contents.
evidence: Phase 4 ends with 'Never report success while ... fail. Fix, re-check, and only then report; state what was run and its outcome.'
There is no report template or enumerated report fields (route, files changed, build/render/inspect results, remaining warnings).
judging basis: consensus-fail

subcomponents.title: Presentation code and tests

criteria.rationale: Every selector in the presentation-owned stylesheet is scoped under the .htmp root class. This includes the kit hooks and the rules inside the @media block. The presentation's Talk applies className="htmp", and the template stylesheet scopes under __PREFIX__.
evidence: presentation.css: every rule begins with `.htmp ` (e.g. `.htmp [data-presentation-attribution]`, `.htmp button`, `.htmp [data-kind=...]`), and the @media (max-width: 600px) rules are also `.htmp ...`…
Talk.tsx passes className="htmp" to Presentation.
presentation.css.tmpl scopes every rule under `.__PREFIX__`.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: Props are properly typed (EntityProps extends HTMLMotionProps<'div'>, and Icon/label/symbol are stripped before the DOM). But Entity spreads {...rest} after layoutId, data-presentation-node and data-presentation-id, so callers can override the kit's identity hooks. layoutId is not omitted from HTMLMotionProps.
evidence: Entity.tsx: <motion.div layout layoutId={id} transition=... data-presentation-node={kind} data-presentation-id={id} style=... {...rest}> puts caller props last.
EntityProps omits only 'id' and 'children' from HTMLMotionProps<'div'>, so a caller can pass layoutId or data-presentation-id and win.
Label and Emphasis forward props straight to Entity, so they inherit the override; the bootstrap template copy has the same ordering.
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: The E2E-003 browser test sleeps for a fixed 200 ms on each step and does not poll for step state. It presses ArrowRight at the end of each iteration and then sleeps, so it asserts without waiting for the step index to advance.
evidence: tests/integration/e2e.test.ts line 114: `await page.waitForTimeout(200)` inside the per-step loop, before page.evaluate measurements.
Line 134 presses ArrowRight with no waitForFunction or expect.poll on data-step-index afterwards.
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: Tests that start a preview use startPreview, which picks a free port dynamically. Each preview is stopped and its browser closed in finally blocks. Verify runs in tests are checked for a closed port afterwards.
evidence: preview.mjs freePort() listens on port 0 and startPreview passes it with --strictPort; no test hardcodes a port.
e2e.test.ts E2E-003 and bootstrap.test.ts call startPreview, then `finally { await browser.close(); preview.stop() }`.
preview.stop() SIGKILLs the node vite process itself (not an npm wrapper).
e2e.test.ts fault tests assert `portClosed(origin)` after verify.mjs exits.
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Verified candidate-produced testing evidence

criteria.rationale: The only exploration in the final round was reproducing F-001 and F-002 at 390×844 on one sample (steps 6 and 9). The log says no other viewports, browsers, touch devices, scaffold or skill journeys, or automated suites were exercised. The ledger confirms the AT-001, AT-002 and AT-004 skill journeys were not run, and it calls them feasible, so the gap is not environmental. Most approved scenarios have no recorded observation in the packet: morphing and entering/exiting entities, persistent grouped scenes, present/browse toggle, keyboard/swipe/jump navigation, boundary clamping, requirement gathering, scaffold, create/modify, and render-failure reporting. The omissions are disclosed but not environmental, and they leave a substantial share of user-visible behavior unexercised.
evidence: Exploration log: 'Deliberately not exercised' lists other viewports, browsers, touch devices, scaffold/skill journeys and automated suites.
Final handoff: the same not-exercised list; zero additional exploration steps.
Ledger: AT-001/AT-002/AT-004 agent journeys 'were NOT run' and are feasible, so skipping them is not an environmental impediment.
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: The round-2 reproductions of F-001 and F-002 are backed by DOM geometry in the log and verified screenshots. Several other material claims have no artifact. The ledger says verification at SHA 1e99777 toggled to browse mode and a malformed caption failed at 'phase=render step=0'. This maps to 'Sample exists and matches the outline' and 'Step error fails verification', and no log or output backs it. The ledger also says the current fixture emitted the expected indistinct-active-chrome warning. This maps to 'Indistinct active chrome is reported', and no fixture or output is recorded. The ledger says AXI confirmed present-mode behavior at index 5, and that an E2E-003 browser test fails against the old footer and passes with the fix. Neither has a recorded command output. Most per-step screenshots are flagged defective for missing capture metadata, with no accompanying observations.
evidence: Ledger 'Current-revision recheck' asserts the caption-validation and active-chrome results without any command output or log.
Ledger round 0 triage asserts E2E-003 fails on the old footer and passes on the fix, and the helper reports no warnings at desktop, with no output recorded.
Most screenshots (sample-narrow, sample-wide, diagnostic-*) are marked defective for missing capture metadata and no record describes them.
judging basis: consensus-fail

criteria.rationale: The recorded tested revision c04536e is the final revision. The harness lists zero product, test-only and harness changes since it, and the tracked diff is empty.
evidence: The tested-revision artifact records c04536e5c11aa266ec7950b1c6b3dcdea3e0330e with relation 'final'.
The lineage facts show changes_to_final counts of 0 for product, test-only and harness files.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The record is candid. It reports NOT READY, keeps F-002 open, and states the zero-exploration budget and everything not exercised. It discloses that CI is absent (only a draft-skipped CodeRabbit context), that the wait-ci checker failed, and that the AXI screenshot timed out and a stale ref occurred. It says the helper's zero warnings do not evaluate legibility. It does not claim that unrun journeys passed. The ledger flags overstated 'done' outcomes and calls the missing agent journeys unmet. I found no demonstrably false or overstated claim, and the unbacked ledger assertions are scored under usable proof.
evidence: Handoff headline: 'NOT READY', and F-002 remains open.
Log and handoff disclose absent CI, the checker failure, harness incidents and not-exercised areas.
Handoff notes that the helper's zero warnings do not evaluate text legibility.
judging basis: consensus-pass

subcomponents.title: Observable assumption handling

criteria.rationale: The record shows two deviations or gaps: the narrow-viewport label unreadability (F-002) and the footer title clipping (F-001). It also shows the unspecified present-mode progress-dot behavior. F-002 is logged as a finding, reproduced, and given a decision entry with options. The footer clip was found, fixed, and re-verified as closed. The present-mode dots are recorded as a ledger entry. Earlier verifier and helper defects are recorded as fixed and rechecked on the current SHA. I found no reproduced deviation that the record leaves unsurfaced.
evidence: F-002 is reproduced at 390×844: the canvas is 342×148 px, scale about 0.389, and 11 px text measures about 4 px.
The ledger holds a 'Round 0 triage of F-002' decision with options 1 and 2, and a separate entry on present-mode progress dots.
The findings file lists F-001 as closed and F-002 as open.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The record separates what the approved spec fixes (an 880×380 canvas scaled uniformly with no reflow) from what it leaves undefined (a minimum legible scale and the narrow strategy). The reproduced F-002 behavior is not called acceptable. It stays an 'open observed defect' that the workflow 'does not claim to meet'. The stale earlier-defect entries are labeled historical and rechecked against the current SHA. The record states that the present-mode dots follow from the spec's 'marker and one-line title' wording and does not claim the spec says more than it does.
evidence: The ledger says: 'Until then F-002 remains an open observed defect against the readability expectation.'
The ledger says: 'this implementation does not claim to meet the AT-003 narrow-readability expectation.'
The ledger's current-revision recheck says the earlier verify and active-chrome issues did not reproduce at SHA 1e99777.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The workflow made no unilateral product decision on the F-002 narrow-composition question. It escalated that question to the user with two options and their consequences. Those options are accepting uniform scaling, or approving a portrait canvas or a minimum-scale rule with a stated threshold. The footer clipping was a clear defect, so the workflow fixed it and added regression tests. The present-mode dots follow the spec's wording, and the ledger says a change would need a user decision. The workflow did not classify any reproduced violation as acceptable or as optional hardening.
evidence: The F-002 triage lists 'Decision needed from the user' with options 1 and 2.
The ledger explains why no code change was made: each remedy conflicts with 'does not reflow' or with the approved per-step design.
F-001 was fixed and covered by a unit assertion and by E2E-003.
judging basis: consensus-pass

criteria.rationale: The handoff names the F-002 narrow-readability decision and points to the ledger. It leaves out other open items and limitations that the ledger itself records. One is the present-mode progress-dot ambiguity, which the ledger calls unspecified, with a spec-change question if the user wants the dots kept. Another is the ledger's statement that the AT-001/002/004 agent journeys are Required but were not run, which it calls a blocking gap. A third is the missing generation-provenance evidence for the reference sample. The handoff says only that 'existing unresolved legibility threshold and narrow-composition questions remain' and that this pass added no new ambiguity. It also gives no option summary of its own.
evidence: The handoff's Assumptions section mentions only the legibility threshold and narrow-composition questions.
The ledger records the present-mode progress dots as unspecified in the 'Acceptance round 0' entry and the 'Round 0 triage' entry.
The ledger says 'Implementation cannot be claimed complete without the agent journeys' and that the sample provenance part is 'missing evidence'.
The handoff's 'Not exercised' list does not mention the sample-provenance gap or the Required AT journeys.
judging basis: consensus-fail

Every ID member and the cardId/linkId helpers are consumed as an id by a rendered element.

votes.rationale: computeScale returns one factor, min(availW/designW, availH/designH), floored at MIN_SCALE. votes.rationale: The port is reserved by freePort(), which closes the listener before spawn, so the port is released and can be taken by another process. Readiness comes from HTTP polling with fetch, not from the child's own announcement, and the child's stdout is 'ignore'. The only ownership check is `child.exitCode !== null`, sampled at the top of each loop iteration before the fetch. A stale or foreign server answering on that port would return res.ok before the child's exit is observed. This is neither accepted mechanism: there is no announced address and no race against child exit.

scene-kit.rationale: computeScale returns one factor, min(availW/designW, availH/designH) floored at 0.3. Stage applies it as transform: scale() on the fixed-size canvas, so the internal composition does not reflow. The available box is the viewport minus the same STAGE_LAYOUT insets that Stage uses to position the stage area, so the fit uses the stage's real bounds. At 1280×720 browse, avail is 1232×456 and scale is 1.2, giving a 1056×456 canvas that fits. At 390×844 browse, avail is 342×580 and scale is about 0.389, giving a 342×148 canvas that fits. Present mode fits with its smaller reserves.

votes.rationale: computeScale returns one factor, min(availW/designW, availH/designH), floored at MIN_SCALE. Stage applies it as transform: scale(s) on the fixed-size canvas, so the internal composition is never reflowed. The available area is the viewport minus the same STAGE_LAYOUT insets that position the stage area, so the fit uses the stage's real bounds. At 1280×720 browse, avail is 1232×456 and the scale is 1.2. At 390×844 browse, avail is 342×580 and the scale is about 0.389, a 342×148 canvas that fits. Present mode fits too, with avail 1232×568 and 342×692. The browse footer stays under its 200px reserve at 1280×720 with the sample CSS (about 178px, estimated by hand).

votes.rationale: computeScale returns a single factor, max(MIN_SCALE, min(availW/designW, availH/designH)). availW and availH are the viewport minus the STAGE_LAYOUT reservations for the current mode. votes.rationale: The port is reserved by freePort(), which closes the listener before spawn, so the port is released and can be taken by another process. Readiness comes from HTTP polling with fetch, not from the child's own announcement, and the child's stdout is 'ignore'. The only ownership check is `child.exitCode !== null`, sampled at the top of each loop iteration before the fetch. A stale or foreign server answering on that port would return res.ok before the child's exit is observed. This is neither accepted mechanism: there is no announced address and no race against child exit.
